subject: Migration intent and hosting constraints — risk matrix & POC next steps
messages:
From: Alex Morales <alex.morales@finserv.co>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finserv.co>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's intro — migration intent and constraints

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the call earlier — good overview. A quick recap from our side and a few clarifying items so we can scope the internal ask:  

- Current environment: self-hosted cluster (on-prem GPUs) running a combination of an older open LLM fork + a commercial vendor API for some endpoints. We average ~1200 inference requests/min during peak, with spiky bursts around batch payroll runs.
- Primary drivers for looking at Redwood: consistent latency (<150ms p95 for single-turn chat), predictable unit cost, and easier rollout for compliance (SOC2 + EU data residency).
- Strong preference for private VPC or on-prem if we have to keep any PII inside our network; otherwise Dedicated would be acceptable if we can get strict data isolation and an SLA.
- Timeline: procurement wants a Q3 POC and procurement approval by end of July.
- Questions we couldn't resolve on the call:  
  1) What does the migration path look like from our current hybrid setup (self-host + vendor API)? Any lift-and-shift options or adapters you provide?
  2) For Private (VPC/on-prem), what does the delivery model look like for our infra team? Is there an appliance/installer or do we manage containers?
  3) Cost: ballpark delta between Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private for an object of our scale — we need something to feed into the internal budget worksheet.

Also looping in Procurement (cc) to keep them in the thread. I can share cluster utilization stats — attaching a small export.

Thanks,
Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
FinServ Co

[Attachment: cluster-stats-Apr2027.csv (text/csv, 42KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morales <alex.morales@finserv.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@finserv.co>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's intro — migration intent and constraints

Alex — thanks for the clear recap and for the export. Looping Marissa (CS lead) and Ben (solutions) to scope a pragmatic path. Quick answers inline, then proposed next steps:  

On your questions:  
1) Migration path from hybrid: we typically run two parallel approaches depending on risk appetite — a) adapter layer + traffic-split to redirect a portion of traffic to Redwood (fast low-risk canary), b) lift-and-shift model artifacts + conversions for quantized weights when moving models to Dedicated/Private. For customers using a commercial API for some endpoints, we can proxy calls to avoid changing callers during an initial POC.

2) Private delivery model: two options — VPC-managed Private (Redwood control plane, customer VPC peering, customer retains KMS keys) or fully air-gapped on-prem package (installer + ops runbook). The on-prem package is delivered as a container bundle plus an orchestrator script; your infra team will run the deployment but we provide a runbook and optional 3-day onsite/remote onboarding.

3) Ballpark cost: rough order-of-magnitude numbers we use for scoping (very rough): Hosted API (metered): $0.0009–$0.003/token depending on model family and volume; Dedicated (reserved): commitment-based monthly starting ~$40k/mo for a mid-size pool; Private (on-prem) is typically licensing + support — upfront platform fee plus annual support (ranges widely based on cluster size). We can produce a detailed pricing scenario once we get token estimates and expected concurrency.

Proposed next steps:  
- Ben to run a short benchmark on a representative payload set (can run against a hosted test instance) — Ben, can you confirm available windows next week?
- Karthik/Marissa to draft a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with milestones (POC kickoff, procurement review, canary cutover) — sending a MAP draft to start (attached).
- Procurement: if you can share the procurement timeline and any standard legal redlines, we can preempt. Procurement, is there an NDA request?

I'll attach the MAP draft and the SOC2 report link for your security team.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: MAP-draft-FinServ.pdf (application/pdf)]
[Link: https://www.redwood.ai/soc2-report]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morales <alex.morales@finserv.co>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@finserv.co>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's intro — migration intent and constraints

Alex — quick technical notes from the bench engineering side and a suggested low-risk POC approach:  

- Bench assumptions: please confirm the most common request shapes (avg tokens in/out), concurrency target, and any required model family (open Llama/Redwood-curated or commercial). The CSV you sent is helpful; could you add a sample JSON payload (headers + example request body) so we can mirror the real call?

- Migration mechanics: when moving models off a vendor API, two common patterns we recommend:  
  a) Proxy/canary: keep your current API layer, add a proxy that routes X% of traffic to Redwood. No code changes for callers.
  b) Containerized model import: export model weights (if licensing allows), run conversion/quantization pipeline we provide, then deploy to Dedicated/Private. Note: quantization tradeoffs can change p95 latency by ~10–30ms depending on model size.

- On-prem installer: the deliverable is a tarball with container images + a deployment script. We do not bundle GPU drivers — your infra team must maintain drivers and CUDA compatible versions. For air-gapped installs we provide a checksum manifest and an offline installer procedure.

- Risk items to flag for your internal risk matrix:  
  * Legal/model licensing: confirm weight redistribution permissions for any open/commercial models.
  * GPU incompatibilities and driver mismatches during on-prem install.
  * Latency variance with quantized runtime (we recommend an A/B run to validate model quality).

Proposed low-risk POC: Redwood-hosted test instance with your sample traffic for 2 weeks, proxying 10–20% of traffic, benchmark p95 and failure modes, then evaluate Dedicated capacity sizing. This gives procurement a data point for the budget worksheet.

Ping me times you have for a 60-min bench kickoff — I can run a scripted workload and hand you the perf/trace outputs (traces include token-level cost and latency breakdown).

- Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
